message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Sub‑genre / Notable Features |
|------|-------|------------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (Alfred Hitchcock) | Psychological thriller, iconic shower scene |
| 1978 | **Halloween** (John Carpenter) | Slasher, introduces Michael Myers |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | Psychological horror, supernatural isolation |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (Wes Craven) | Dream‑based slasher, Freddy Krueger |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (Jonathan Demme) | Psychological thriller, cannibalistic serial killer |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Found‑footage, folklore horror |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | Post‑apocalyptic, fast‑moving infected |
| 2004 | **Saw** (James Wan & Leigh Whannell) | Psychological horror, intricate traps |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (Oren Peli) | Found‑footage, supernatural hauntings |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | Paranormal investigation, real‑life inspiration |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (Dennis Dugan) | Meta‑horror, subverts tropes |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (David Robert Mitchell) | Creepy, supernatural curse |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (Robert Eggers) | Period horror, atmospheric dread |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | Social satire, psychological horror |
| 2018 | **Hereditary** (Ari Aster) | Family trauma, supernatural dread |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | Daylight horror, cult rituals |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (Leigh Whannell) | Modern retelling, psychological terror |
| 2021 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | Silence‑based horror, family survival |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (Scott Derrickson) | Supernatural thriller, telephones |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (Zack Snyder) | AI horror, psychological twist |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre or era!
